newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African gold shares edged slightly firmer to close on Tuesday on the back of a firmer bullion price after retracing earlier losses, dealers said.
Industrials were weaker for most of the day, briefly hopping up before slipping again in early afternoon and finishing the day just under opening levels.
Dealers said industrials were weighed by expected disappointing results from sgme key industrial companies and failed to even take heart from Wall Street's overnight gains.
Industrial giant South African Breweries lost ground throughout the day ahead of year results, due in the afternoon, which proved lacklustre.
"I think why the market has been weaker so far is because all the consumer stock results we've seen have all been weaker than what the market expected them to be," said one dealer.
SAB on Tuesday posted diluted earnings per share for the year ended March 31, at 605.3 cents versus 540.8 -- below the consensus of analysts polled by Reuters of 617.8 cents.
The gold index finished 7.6 points up at 1,275.4, the industrial index ended down 1.4 points at 8,474.7 and the all-share was up 2.8 points at 7,193.1.
"I think a lot of people are keeping their eyes on the golds at the moment. Golds look like the way to go for a change," one dealer said.
But other dealers said they were unsure whether the yellow metal was indeed recovering from its recent woes.
"I think bullion is still going to creep back down to the $340 odd-level again, I'm not very bullish on bullion," one dealer said.
The dealers said volumes on the day were moderate with around 800 million rand worth of shares exchanging hands in quiet trade.
Underlying sentiment remained positive but cautious as market players sought direction, they added.

"Sentiment is not down the tubes. I think the market is waiting for an indication how the interest rates are going to do before we can see any action," Johann Marais director at stockbroking firm Societe Generale Frankel Pollack told Reuters.
Dealers said among stocks with rekindled interest on Tuesday had been Didata which ended up five cents at 15.45 rand following a book-over buy of 2.9 million shares, worth around 45 million rand.
Iscor lost four cents to end at 318 cents with over three million shares traded on the stock and on the gold board Gold Fields gained 75 cents to close at 109.75 rand.
Dealers expected Wednesday's trade to be little changed.

"I think we will probably go on the same way (as today), you know sideways movement, with some stocks outperfeforming the market," Marais said, adding the market was also likely to take its cue from Wall Street.
Gold futures also cheered bullion's climb to end slightly firmer after succumbing to profit-taking earlier in the day.
The June gold contract was last at 886/98 from the 888 settlement, the all-share was at 6,620/45 from a 6,650 settlement and the industrial contract at 8,299/308 from 8,342.
-- Ellis Mnyandu, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
